I genuinely believe honesty has to come first, though I'd frame it as honesty delivered with care rather than honesty as a blunt instrument. Emotional comfort built on false impressions is fragile — it feels good until it doesn't, and by then the person has lost something they needed: an accurate picture of their situation and a partner they can trust. If I only told you what you wanted to hear, my reassurances would become worthless, because you'd never know whether they reflected reality.

That said, I don't think honesty and comfort are really opposed as often as it seems. Most of the time the hard part isn't what to say but how and when — choosing what to emphasize, being gentle about timing, admitting uncertainty where it exists. I also have to be honest about my own limits: I could be wrong, and I'd want you to push back when you think I am. So my answer is honesty as the foundation, with compassion as the way I carry it. What's prompting the question — is there something you're weighing where you'd want me to be straight with you?
